correctness.rationale: An invertible odd-cycle modular-center/difference transform maps four equally likely joint nearest-neighbor moves to an isotropic lazy two-dimensional walk killed at zero difference. Fourier decomposition in center yields an exactly solved two-boundary recurrence with a hyperbolic-cosine expression. Joint geometric resets yield a renewal ratio for every collision-location Fourier coefficient and a renewal quotient for its mean. First and factorial-second-moment discrete Poisson equations prove the exact weak-reset derivative, including the finite-size correction. The standalone program independently verifies the complete absorbing location vector and mean against the original ordered-pair chain, plus derivative checks, in 242 finite comparisons; its finite experiments do not prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: The full first-collision site distribution is a natural missing reaction-location observable not given by prescribed-target means. The Fourier reduction gives all sites and all reset rates in a single explicit formula. The finite-size weak-reset phase criterion has a physically nontrivial parity reversal: two-step-separated initial walkers on C5 accelerate under weak joint reset while adjacent initial walkers slow down, despite the reverse intuitive ranking by Euclidean separation. This is a motivated structural and design result rather than a perturbative numerical increment; no paper-sized downstream application is required.
